text:
Maya (ML Eng): quick thread — want to align on cross-val sensitivity tests for onboarding Orion-12B (gguf) across int8 / fp8 / baseline fp16. specific ask: recommended minimal probe set + acceptance thresholds for early rollback?
Simon (ML Research): +1. suggest 3 probes: core prompt set (200), long-tail (50 long contexts), and rerank tasks (50). acceptance: <= 1.5% delta on our reward score and <= 2% latency regression.
Jules (Infra): note infra limits — we have 2 p4d nodes free next week, can run calibration in parallel but ffwd quantization jobs will need gguf I/O tuning.
Liam (Prod Eng): cost note: int8 -> ~0.45x token cost vs fp16, fp8 -> ~0.6x. perf numbers from earlier runs: int8 latency +5-10ms, fp8 +2-4ms.
QuantBot: queued eval harness: /evals/run?model=orion-12b.gguf&trial=int8&shots=0&seed=42 — status: scheduled.
Maya (ML Eng): for the probe set, I'm proposing: 200 short completion prompts (mean len 32), 50 long-context (mean len 2048), 50 instruction-style multi-turn checks. We'll capture: reward_score, exact-match on structured outputs, sacreBLEU for code, and token-level likelihood drift.
Simon (ML Research): also run temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7) and top_p (0.9) — calibration can hide or amplify regressions. include calibration sample seeds and record per-token perplexity delta.
Maya (ML Eng): here's a quick command to run calibration locally (use infra wrapper in prod):
```
python tools/quant_calib.py \
  --model artifacts/orion-12b.gguf \
  --precision int8 \
  --calib-samples 1024 \
  --batch 16 \
  --out /tmp/calib_int8.json
```
Simon (ML Research): add `--probe-set data/probes/sensitivity_v2.jsonl` and `--metrics reward,perplexity,exact_match` to the job. Also log token distribution histogram.
Jules (Infra): note: when reading gguf from NFS we saw occasional spikes — pin to local SSD for calibration. will add a job label `local-ssd=true`. @Maya can you mark the runs that must use SSD?
Maya (ML Eng): will do. also let's record memory high-water mark and kv-cache footprint; for fp8 we saw ~10% memory reduction vs fp16, good to capture.
Liam (Prod Eng): FYI we have a quick fallback plan: if int8 reward drop > 2% on core prompts, auto-fallback to fp8 variant in rollout config. I can wire that into the canary policy.
Simon (ML Research): decision matrix suggestion: prefer int8 if reward delta <= 1% and latency improvement > 5% and cost < 0.6x. prefer fp8 if reward delta in (1%,2%) but still cost savings. else stick to fp16.
Maya (ML Eng): timeline: I'll queue int8 sensitivity runs Monday morning on the 2 p4ds (priority). Simon will run fp8 overnights and send aggregated diffs. Jules will prepare SSD-backed job queue.
QuantBot: job 3298765432-int8-calib queued on p4d-02. ETA: 3h.
Maya (ML Eng): great — after the runs we'll produce a 1-page decision note: metrics, per-prompt outliers, sample-regression examples, and rollout recommendation. tagging @Simon @Liam for signoff. :thumbsup:
Simon (ML Research): acknowledged. I'll add a small ablation to check weight folding impact on int8 rounding.
Jules (Infra): will monitor IO and memory; ping me if jobs fail.
Liam (Prod Eng): once Maya posts the decision note I'll draft canary config and cost delta estimate.
Maya (ML Eng): thanks all — ending thread, will post results in same thread when available.
